Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and Order Form and attached a redline (Synergos_MSA_redlines_v3.docx). The main open items for us are around:

- Output ownership: your standard clause appears to grant Redwood broad rights over model outputs. We need explicit confirmation that Synergos retains ownership of customer-specific outputs and derivatives we create using the service.
- Training/data use: the MSA currently allows using customer content for model improvement. We need to limit that to aggregated/non-identifying metrics or have an explicit opt-out.
- Feedback/telemetry license: can you clarify the scope (revocable, exclusive/non-exclusive) and whether there are any perpetual rights being requested.

I've highlighted suggested edits in the attached doc. Can your legal team review and propose alternative language that balances your product-improvement needs with our confidentiality and IP concerns? We have a target signature this month.

Also cc'ing procurement for timeline coordination.

Regards,
Ava Collins

Hi all,

I reviewed Synergos' redlines and added suggested language (attached: redline_suggestions.docx). High level recommendations:

1) Output ownership: we can accept customer ownership of "Customer Outputs" where outputs are unmodified content produced for the customer. We need a clear definition in the MSA that excludes (a) model weights/derivatives that constitute a product competed into a model offering, and (b) aggregated statistical derivatives. Proposed approach:
- Define "Customer Output" = text, embeddings, artifacts produced by the Service in response to Customer Input, excluding model artifacts and aggregated metrics.
- Confirm a narrow license back to Redwood solely to reproduce outputs for the purpose of serving the Customer and debugging. This should be non-exclusive and revocable on termination for derivative uses.

2) Training/data use: Redwood is comfortable with using de-identified, aggregated telemetry to improve models, but we should offer a customer opt-out. For Synergos we can propose:
- Default: Redwood may use aggregated, non-identifying telemetry and synthetic benchmarks.
- Opt-out: Customer may check an option in the Order Form to prohibit using Customer Input and Customer Outputs for model training.

3) Feedback license: limit to a non-exclusive, perpetual (technical note: we often request perpetual for engineering efficiency) but non-transferable license to use feedback internally for service improvement. If Synergos prefers revocable or time-limited, propose a compromise of a revocable license with a 12-month automatic expiration unless extended.

We should also propose specific redline text for the Order Form to allow customers to select the training opt-out and to confirm output ownership for specific deliverables. See attached for exact wording.

If this approach sounds acceptable to you both, Laura, I can prepare the one-page Order Form patch you can send to Ava for sign-off.

—Kar
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed compromise language & Order Form patch for Synergos

Hi Ava — following up with the compromise language Kar drafted and an Order Form patch that implements the training opt-out and confirms customer output ownership for specified deliverables. I attached the patch (proposed_orderform_patch.json) and included the key points below:

Key points in the patch:
- Customer Output: defined as response artifacts produced by the Service in response to Customer Input; Customer retains ownership of these outputs.
- License to Redwood: non-exclusive, limited to reproduction/serving and debugging; no rights to incorporate Customer Outputs into model weights or productized model derivatives without separate written consent.
- Training & Use of Data: default allowed for aggregated, de-identified telemetry only. The Order Form includes a checkbox "Prohibit use of Customer Content for training" — if selected, Customer Input and Customer Outputs will not be used for model training.
- Feedback License: limited, non-transferable license to use feedback internally; license revokes automatically 12 months after termination unless extended.

Ask: can you confirm if this addresses Synergos' concerns? If so, we can add the Order Form checkbox and prepare a countersign-ready Order Form while Kar finishes MSA redlines. If you want the feedback license revocable immediately on termination (rather than 12 months), call that out and we can patch.

DocuSign/next steps: once you confirm language, I can generate a countersignable Order Form and send via DocuSign.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
